Begin with one useful program.

Starting from zero? Open the app and choose Today → Start this lesson. The six guided foundation days grow a Python study-budget calculator from a saved file into a validated command-line tool. Then explore a career route in Path.

A study day is a budget, not a deadline. The default foundation plan reserves 360 active minutes, with 90 break minutes additional. Spread the work across more calendar days when needed. Six foundation days are an on-ramp, not a job-readiness promise.

The sections below group related subjects; they are not one fixed execution order. Prerequisites cross section boundaries. Follow the linked modules and your chosen route in the app. The app also contains the full explanations, exercises, worked examples, and transfer checks.

Start from zero

Guided foundation days

Build one program in deliberate steps. Record what you can explain and carry unfinished work forward.

Guided day 01

Make a saved file do useful arithmetic

Save, run, test, and explain a Python study-budget calculator that distinguishes active study from elapsed time.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Guided day 02

Turn typed text into measured quantities

Build an interactive minute-budget calculator and express totals as whole hours plus remaining minutes.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Guided day 03

Make decisions and reject impossible ranges

Validate integer time ranges, enforce a chosen 24-hour planning window, and print one correct target classification.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Guided day 04

Repeat useful work without copying it

Collect repeated study blocks, maintain a running total, and explain every iteration with a trace table.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Guided day 05

Give a calculation a clear contract

Define, call, test, and explain small functions that return calculated values without collecting input or printing inside them.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Guided day 06

Deliver a small program with an honest test record

Build a three-block planning tool that handles malformed numeric text, validates its constraints, and explains planned, available, and unassigned study time.

Planning budget: 360 active minutes + 90 break minutes. Spread the work over more days when useful.

Research replication and mathematical depth

Read a technical claim as an argument, reconstruct its mathematics and experiment, and reproduce a bounded result before attempting an extension.

Prerequisites: C19 · PyTorch: reliable training as an engineering loop, C21 · Language models from tokens to transformers, B05 · Mathematical depth for research

View five sessions, outcomes, and project for A11

Learning sessions

  1. Read a paper as a structured argument
  2. Connect equations to tensor operations
  3. Build a reproducible experiment before scaling
  4. Design one ablation that can answer a question
  5. Explain discrepancies and communicate limits

What you will demonstrate

  • Translate a paper into a claim, assumptions, algorithm, and evaluation protocol.
  • Derive a relevant gradient and check it numerically.
  • Run controlled replications and report discrepancies, uncertainty, and negative results.

Module projectA small, honest replication study

A12

Portfolio evidence and a global job-search practice

Translate demonstrated ability into a clear portfolio, evaluate current job requirements systematically, and practice communicating technical decisions.

Prerequisites: C15 · Evaluation: decisions, uncertainty, and calibration

View five sessions, outcomes, and project for A12

Learning sessions

  1. Sample the market as data, not as a slogan
  2. Build an evidence map for one target role
  3. Write a case study that survives inspection
  4. Practice interviews as observable reasoning
  5. Run an ethical application and improvement loop

What you will demonstrate

  • Analyze a dated sample of relevant job postings without claiming it represents the entire global market.
  • Package a role-specific capstone with reproducible evidence and honest limitations.
  • Practice technical explanations, problem solving, applications, and feedback-driven iteration.

Module projectAn evidence-backed career dossier

B05

Mathematical depth for research

Translate derivatives, constraints, estimators and information objectives into small experiments whose assumptions and conclusions can be inspected.

Prerequisites: C08 · Linear algebra as geometry and computation, C09 · Probability as reasoning under uncertainty, C10 · Statistics, experiments, and causal restraint, C19 · PyTorch: reliable training as an engineering loop

View five sessions, outcomes, and project for B05

Learning sessions

  1. Derive a vector gradient and test its direction
  2. Separate constraints from poor conditioning
  3. Study estimators as repeated procedures
  4. Connect information objectives to probability assumptions
  5. Design a mathematical claim that code can challenge

What you will demonstrate

  • Derive vector gradients with explicit shapes and check them through directional perturbations
  • Distinguish constraints, curvature, conditioning and numerical precision in optimization behavior
  • Explain estimator bias, variance and uncertainty without treating a finite simulation as proof
  • Connect cross-entropy and KL divergence to an explicit probability model and support assumptions
  • Produce a reproducible mathematical experiment with baselines, falsifiable predictions and bounded conclusions

Module projectA derivation-to-experiment research notebook
